summary: Roland Ferenczi is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. Attested in 2026, he held posts as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University and as a wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter at the University of Hamburg.
Roland Steiner works in Indology and Tibetology. He studied under Michael Hahn (attested 1990) and held an assistant professorship at the University of Marburg, attested in 2002.

Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who earned his doctorate from the University of Salzburg in 2002 and his habilitation at Heidelberg University. His posts include positions at Heidelberg University, the University of Basel, and a professorship at the University of Munich (2017).

Rolf Alfred Stein was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen, INALCO, and EPHE, serving as directeur d'études at EPHE (1951–1975) and professor at the Collège de France (1965–1982).
Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, attested in 2010, under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher.

Romila Thapar is a historian of ancient India. She earned degrees from Panjab University, the University of the Punjab, and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. She was a professor at the University of Delhi and Jawaharlal Nehru University.
Ron Garry is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and under Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer (1932–2017) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under the traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. His academic appointments include Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland, attested in 1998, and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and management who studied under traditional teacher Koshin Ogui in 1985. He held posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1989–1995) and San Francisco State University (~1995).

Ronald Egan is a Sinologist who completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University (~1971–1977). He held appointments at Harvard, Wellesley College, the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1993–2012), and Stanford University (~2012–2021).

Ronald Eric Emmerick (1937–2001) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at Oxford under Harold Walter Bailey and held posts at SOAS (~1964–1971) and the University of Hamburg (1971–2001).

Ronald Inden is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Chicago, where he is attested in 2026 as Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations.

Ronald M. Davidson works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (1985), studying under numerous teachers, and held academic posts at Fairfield University, attested between 2002 and 2014.
Ronald Neufeldt is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He spent his academic career at the University of Calgary from circa 1977 to 2006, where he became Professor Emeritus in 2006.

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1974–1980). He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1987–2000) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).
Rong Geng (1894–1983) was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Peking University (~1922–1925) and served on the faculty at Yenching University (~1926–1941).

Rongdao Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She completed her PhD at McGill University (attested 2013) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, later becoming Assistant Professor there (attested 2026).

Ronit Ricci is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1994–1999) and held posts at the Australian National University (~2007–2013) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2013).

Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.
